findings.description: The EBS volume attached to the portal server does not set encrypted = true or a kms_key_id, so data written to this additional disk is stored unencrypted. Any snapshot or volume recovery would expose cleartext data.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet (including aws_instance.portal_server) to receive a public IP, and the subnet is associated with a route table that has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, placing workloads directly on the public internet.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances in this subnet, which is routed to the internet gateway via aws_route_table.portal_routes, removing the network boundary for any workload placed here.

A 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway is applied to the single route table associated with both subnets, so there is no private/segmented tier in this VPC; all hosts are directly internet-reachable and can reach the internet outbound.

The instance user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the host (including via SSRF), and the secret is stored unencrypted in the launch configuration and Terraform state.
Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts against the portal server.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with no corresponding TLS (443) listener, so all traffic to the web server is transmitted unencrypted over untrusted networks.
Egress allows all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound segmentation and permitting data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised instance.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.
No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, leaving the instance metadata service accessible via IMDSv1, which is exploitable through SSRF to steal instance credentials.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.
No public access block, bucket ACL restriction, or bucket policy denying public access is configured for the flow log archive, risking unintended public exposure of network logs.
The bucket has no policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport, allowing objects to be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
force_destroy = true permits deletion of the bucket and all stored flow logs without safeguards, undermining the integrity and availability of audit/network evidence.

The EBS snapshot is created from aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk without any encryption enforcement declared; if the source volume is unencrypted the snapshot stores the portal server's disk contents in cleartext, and snapshots are easily shared/copied across accounts.

The network interface defines no security_groups argument, so it falls back to the VPC default security group instead of the purpose-built aws_security_group.portal_sg, bypassing the intended network boundary controls for this interface.
